third_party.changes: mesh split into one node per physical control with pivots; re-based into the GoldenEye joypad model frame (GjoypadZ) and scaled to its 788-unit width; normal / metallic-roughness / emissive maps dropped; base-colour textures resized to 1024 px and re-encoded as PNG; manufacturer logos removed (button symbols and letters kept); the four face-button symbols (cross, circle, triangle, square) on the button-top tile darkened and thickened by script (tools/asset/darken_symbols.py, see sightline_edits); the button-top material given alphaMode MASK (cutoff 0.5) so its clear-coat layering no longer hides the symbols (see sightline_edits); compiled to Sightline's native .slmodel format with a part table

textures/dualsense_basecolor_1.png.why: the symbols were 2..3-texel grey (RGB 159) strokes on the lilac button tops (RGB 231/225/237) and vanished into plain discs at the watch page's ~12 px buttons and ~13 px icons (#63 / #64 round 6)
textures/dualsense_basecolor_1.png.rule: inside each region a texel with luminance 120..205 and channel spread <= 16 is the stroke; the stroke is dilated 3 texels (a disc), at most 6 texels outside the region, onto texels lighter than 205 only; every mask texel is painted RGB 56/56/64, alpha kept; 5080 texels painted, nothing else touched

dualsense.gltf materials[dualsense_mat1].why: the tile's alpha channel is the author's clear-coat layering - each face button carries a cap at alpha ~51 over the symbol face at alpha ~150-160, and 268,847 texels (26%) of the tile are below 128 - exported with no alphaMode, i.e. OPAQUE, so the caps drew solid and hid the symbols and the d-pad arrows (measured on the page: plain discs even with the darkened strokes compiled in)
dualsense.gltf materials[dualsense_mat1].change: alphaMode MASK, alphaCutoff 0.5 (the renderer's alpha test, src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c); BLEND was tried and shows depth-order artefacts (a black button); nothing else in the material changed
dualsense.gltf materials[dualsense_mat1].effect: the symbols and the d-pad arrows read on the page's pad and icons; no other visible change on the page

authored_parts.btn_ps: plain btn_ps replacing the original logo-shaped part

authored_parts_note: These parts are the project owner's own replacement geometry (manufacturer logos removed); everything else in the mesh and every texture is the third party's CC-BY-4.0 work as changed above.
debranding: btn_ps: the logo-shaped button (all five shells) replaced by an owner-authored plain oval covering the logo-shaped recess so no outline shows through (extras.sl_authored_part on the node); tile 1002 (textures/dualsense_basecolor_2.png): the manufacturer wordmark painted out with the surrounding colour (the tile is now one flat colour, zero dark pixels).
frame: GjoypadZ: +x = player's right, +y = up toward the watch camera, -z = the top edge; N64 body 788 x 253 x 836; fitted to width 788
parts_note: package node label (extras.sl_part) -> canonical physical part (tools/asset/gltf_import.py PARTS); physical controls only, never actions
